spec.title: Deep Determinants of Growth and Classical Macro Growth Theory

activities.title: Introduction: The Puzzle of Long-Run Growth
activities.learnerDoes: Listen and take notes; respond to guiding questions about why some countries are rich and others poor, and what 'deep determinants' might mean.
activities.teacherDoes: Pose the motivating question of cross-country income differences; preview the objective: explain deep determinants of growth and classical macro growth theory; outline the session.

activities.title: Classical Growth Theory: Smith, Malthus, and Ricardo
activities.learnerDoes: In small groups, read short excerpts from Mankiw's textbook on classical growth theory and compare the Malthusian trap, diminishing returns, and the role of land; then present one key mechanism to the class.
activities.teacherDoes: Provide excerpts and a comparison chart; clarify the logic of classical theory; connect to the idea of deep determinants (geography, institutions, culture) as extensions of classical constraints.

activities.title: Solow-Swan Model as a Bridge to Deep Determinants
activities.learnerDoes: Work through a guided numerical example of the Solow-Swan model from the teacher's notes; identify how saving, population growth, and technology affect steady-state output; discuss what the model leaves unexplained (total factor productivity) as a gateway to deep determinants.
activities.teacherDoes: Lectures on the Solow-Swan model using the notes; draws the production function and steady-state diagram; asks students to isolate the 'residual' and links it to deep determinants such as institutions and geography.

activities.title: Schools of Thought: Comparing Classical, Neoclassical, and New Growth Perspectives
activities.learnerDoes: Using a teacher-provided timeline of economic thought, sort key propositions into classical, neoclassical, and new growth theory; then discuss which deep determinants each school emphasizes.
activities.teacherDoes: Facilitates a sorting activity and leads a discussion contrasting Malthusian limits, Solow's exogenous technology, and endogenous innovation; clarifies how each school explains persistent growth differences.

activities.title: Synthesis and Written Explanation
activities.learnerDoes: Write a short paragraph explaining the deep determinants of growth (institutions, geography, culture, openness) and how classical growth theory frames the problem; submit the paragraph as a work product.
activities.teacherDoes: Circulates to provide feedback; collects the paragraphs; closes by summarising how classical theory and modern approaches together define deep determinants.
